blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY – Lumad and human rights groups slammed the shortened tribal consent process for projects within ancestral lands, saying it places indigenous peoples (IPs) and their communities on the path to rapid exploitation by business interests like mining corporations. The new rules on the government’s Free and Prior Informed Consent (FPIC) was approved by the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) en banc last May 1 through Administrative Order No. 3, but the revisions were only published on its website recently, including the controversial shorter period granted to IPs to give their consent to projects within their ancestral […]...
